category: currency exchange-rate API (keyless endpoint behind the embeddable widgets: rates, currencies, conversion, VAT rates)

free_tier.stated: Keyless endpoint at api.unirateapi.com/api/widget/v1: 60 requests per minute per IP with no API key, signup or credit card; rates refresh hourly.
free_tier.notes: The widgets page names this endpoint as the data source of its embeddable widgets. GET /widget/v1/rates?base=USD answered the full rate table for a base, fiat and crypto, as JSON; the widget script also calls /widget/v1/currencies, /widget/v1/convert and /widget/v1/vat/all. The keyed Free tier of the same vendor is recorded separately.

per_object_cap.stated: no cap is stated; one rates answer for the base USD was 21969 bytes of JSON

retention.stated: not applicable: a query API with no stored objects; the widget calls serve current rates, currencies, conversions and VAT rates

egress.terms: not metered in bytes; 60 requests a minute per IP bound what an address can pull

interface_detail: GET https://api.unirateapi.com/api/widget/v1/rates?base=USD, /widget/v1/currencies, /widget/v1/convert?amount=&from=&to= and /widget/v1/vat/all with no key; JSON answers carrying x-ratelimit-burst-limit, x-ratelimit-burst-remaining and x-ratelimit-burst-reset headers.
tooling: any HTTP client; the embeddable widget script at unirateapi.com/lander/static/js/unirate-widgets.js calls the same routes
chaining: Keyless current fiat and crypto rates for any base at 60 requests a minute per IP, so a free stack can refresh a rate table hourly without a key; history, time series and metals need the keyed Pro tier of the same vendor or another source.

limits.value: 60 requests per minute per IP, with no authentication; past it the endpoint answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After

limits_note: Current data only: the widget routes cover rates, currencies, conversion and VAT rates, with no history route.
binding_note: The only limit stated is 60 requests a minute per IP.

identity_cost.detail: No key, signup or card: the widgets page says the widget pulls rates from the public endpoint with no key, and a keyless GET answered HTTP 200 with a rates table.

reliability_note: Past the per-minute limit the endpoint answers HTTP 429 with Retry-After 20; it is documented as the data source of the embeddable widgets rather than as a general API, and refreshes hourly.
confidence_note: The keyless HTTP 200 answer, its size, the burst limit of 60 in its headers and the HTTP 429 answer past it are measured; the hourly refresh and the intended use are read from the widgets page.

evidence.proved: the widget needs no API key, signup or credit card and pulls rates from a public endpoint
evidence.quote: No API key, no signup, no credit card — the widget pulls real exchange rates from UniRate's public endpoint the moment the page loads.

evidence.proved: the public endpoint allows 60 requests per minute per IP with no auth
